summary: This section sets limits on what the board of directors can do without asking the shareholders first. The board needs a special resolution from the company to sell major business parts, invest certain merger money in trust securities, borrow past a specific capital limit, or give a director extra time to pay a debt. Without this special permission, some of these actions may not be valid.
points: The board must get a special resolution to sell, lease, or dispose of the whole or substantially the whole of an undertaking.
The board needs a special resolution to invest compensation from a merger into trust securities.
A special resolution is required to borrow money that exceeds the company paid-up share capital, free reserves, and securities premium.
The board needs a special resolution to forgive or give extra time to repay a debt owed by a director.
A special resolution for borrowing must state the total amount of money the board is allowed to borrow.
example: Meera Textiles Private Limited wanted to sell a major factory unit that generated a large share of the company total income. Because this factory counted as a substantial part of the company undertaking, the board of directors could not simply decide to sell it on their own. Instead, the board had to call a meeting and ask the shareholders to pass a special resolution giving their consent. Only after the shareholders agreed through this special vote could Meera Textiles Private Limited move forward with selling the factory unit to the buyer.

terms.meaning: A formal decision made by shareholders with a high required majority vote.
A business unit or part of a company defined by specific investment or income thresholds.
Reserves that are available for distribution as dividends based on the audited balance sheet.
Loans repayable on demand or within a short period, such as cash credits or seasonal short-term loans.

watch: Temporary loans obtained in the ordinary course of business from the company bankers do not count towards the general borrowing limit.
